sanskrit: jñānaṃ niḥśreya ity āhur vṛddhā niścayadarśinaḥ tasmāj jñānena śuddhena mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ
english: The elders who perceive things with certainty declare that knowledge is the highest good; therefore by pure knowledge a man is freed from all his sins.

sanskrit: hiṃsāparāś ca ye loke ye ca nāstikavṛttayaḥ lobhamohasamāyuktās te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those in the world who are devoted to violence, those whose conduct is that of unbelievers, and those bound by greed and delusion—these surely go the way to hell.

sanskrit: āśīryuktāni karmāṇi kurvate ye tv atandritāḥ te 'smiṃl loke pramodante jāyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: But those who untiringly perform actions joined to desire for reward rejoice in this world, being born again and again.

sanskrit: kurvate ye tu karmāṇi śraddadhānā vipaścitaḥ anāśīryogasaṃyuktās te dhīrāḥ sādhudarśinaḥ
english: But those wise and faithful men who perform their actions joined to a discipline free of craving—they are the steadfast ones, seers of the good.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi sattvakṣetrajñayor yathā saṃyogo viprayogaś ca tan nibodhata sattamāḥ
english: Now beyond this I shall declare how the union and the separation of primal matter and the Knower of the Field come about; learn it well, O best of men.

sanskrit: viṣayo viṣayitvaṃ ca saṃbandho 'yam ihocyate viṣayī puruṣo nityaṃ sattvaṃ ca viṣayaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: This is called the relation here: that of the object and of objecthood. The Spirit is ever the experiencing subject, while matter is held to be the object.

sanskrit: vyākhyātaṃ pūrvakalpena maśakodumbaraṃ yathā bhujyamānaṃ na jānīte nityaṃ sattvam acetanam yas tv eva tu vijānīte yo bhuṅkte yaś ca bhujyate
english: This has been explained before by the earlier illustration, as of the gnat and the fig: matter, being unconscious, never knows that it is being enjoyed; but there is one who knows, who enjoys, and who is enjoyed.

sanskrit: anityaṃ dvaṃdvasaṃyuktaṃ sattvam āhur guṇātmakam nirdvaṃdvo niṣkalo nityaḥ kṣetrajño nirguṇātmakaḥ
english: They say matter is impermanent, bound to the pairs of opposites, and made up of the strands of nature; but the Knower of the Field is beyond the pairs, indivisible, eternal, and free of the strands.

sanskrit: samaḥ saṃjñāgatas tv evaṃ yadā sarvatra dṛśyate upabhuṅkte sadā sattvam āpaḥ puṣkaraparṇavat
english: When, having attained this awareness, he is seen as the same everywhere, he ever enjoys matter as the lotus leaf bears the water upon it.

sanskrit: sarvair api guṇair vidvān vyatiṣakto na lipyate jalabindur yathā lolaḥ padminīpatrasaṃsthitaḥ evam evāpy asaṃsaktaḥ puruṣaḥ syān na saṃśayaḥ
english: Though joined with all the strands of nature, the wise man is not stained by them; just as a trembling drop of water rests upon a lotus leaf, even so, beyond doubt, the Spirit remains unattached.

sanskrit: dravyamātram abhūt sattvaṃ puruṣasyeti niścayaḥ yathā dravyaṃ ca kartā ca saṃyogo 'py anayos tathā
english: The certainty is that matter is merely the material substance belonging to the Spirit; as there is substance and an agent, so too there is the union of these two.

sanskrit: yathā pradīpam ādāya kaś cit tamasi gacchati tathā sattvapradīpena gacchanti paramaiṣiṇaḥ
english: As a man takes up a lamp and walks through the darkness, so by the lamp of pure matter the seekers of the supreme make their way.

sanskrit: yāvad dravyaguṇas tāvat pradīpaḥ saṃprakāśate kṣīṇadravyaguṇaṃ jyotir antardhānāya gacchati
english: As long as the quality of the fuel lasts, so long the lamp shines forth; when the quality of the fuel is exhausted, the light passes into extinction.

sanskrit: vyaktaḥ sattvaguṇas tv evaṃ puruṣo 'vyakta iṣyate etad viprā vijānīta hanta bhūyo bravīmi vaḥ
english: Thus the quality of matter is manifest, while the Spirit is held to be unmanifest. Understand this, O brāhmaṇas; come, I shall tell you yet more.

sanskrit: sahasreṇāpi durmedhā na vṛddhim adhigacchati caturthenāpy athāṃśena buddhimān sukham edhate
english: Even with a thousand portions the dull-witted man attains no growth, whereas with but a quarter portion the wise man prospers with ease.

sanskrit: evaṃ dharmasya vijñeyaṃ saṃsādhanam upāyataḥ upāyajño hi medhāvī sukham atyantam aśnute
english: In like manner one should understand the accomplishment of righteousness through right means; for the intelligent man who knows the means enjoys boundless happiness.

sanskrit: yathādhvānam apātheyaḥ prapanno mānavaḥ kva cit kleśena yāti mahatā vinaśyaty antarāpi vā
english: As a man without provisions who sets out upon a road somewhere travels on with great hardship, or even perishes along the way,

sanskrit: tathā karmasu vijñeyaṃ phalaṃ bhavati vā na vā puruṣasyātmaniḥśreyaḥ śubhāśubhanidarśanam
english: so too in the matter of works it must be understood that the fruit may come or may not come; the highest good lies in the Self, which reveals the auspicious and the inauspicious.

sanskrit: yathā ca dīrgham adhvānaṃ padbhyām eva prapadyate adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ sahasā tattvadarśanavarjitaḥ
english: And as one suddenly sets out on foot alone upon a long road never seen before, bereft of any vision of the truth,

sanskrit: tam eva ca yathādhvānaṃ rathenehāśugāminā yāyād aśvaprayuktena tathā buddhimatāṃ gatiḥ
english: and as one might traverse that same road by a swift-going chariot yoked with horses—such is the course of the wise.

sanskrit: uccaṃ parvatam āruhya nānvavekṣeta bhūgatam rathena rathinaṃ paśyet kliśyamānam acetanam
english: Having climbed a high mountain, the charioteer should not look down at the one upon the ground, the dull man toiling along, whom he beholds from his own chariot.

sanskrit: yāvad rathapathas tāvad rathena sa tu gacchati kṣīṇe rathapathe prājño ratham utsṛjya gacchati
english: As far as there is a road fit for the chariot, so far he goes by chariot; but when the chariot-road comes to an end, the wise man abandons the chariot and proceeds on foot.

sanskrit: evaṃ gacchati medhāvī tattvayogavidhānavit samājñāya mahābuddhir uttarād uttarottaram
english: Thus the intelligent man advances, knowing the rule of yoga and the truth; the man of great wisdom, having fully grasped each higher stage, passes from the higher to the still higher.

sanskrit: yathā mahārṇavaṃ ghoram aplavaḥ saṃpragāhate bāhubhyām eva saṃmohād vadhaṃ carcchaty asaṃśayam
english: As a man without a boat who, out of delusion, plunges into the terrible great ocean with his arms alone undoubtedly meets his death,

sanskrit: nāvā cāpi yathā prājño vibhāgajñas taritrayā aklāntaḥ salilaṃ gāhet kṣipraṃ saṃtarati dhruvam
english: so the wise man who knows the distinctions, plunging unwearied into the water by a boat fitted for crossing, surely crosses over quickly.

sanskrit: tīrṇo gacchet paraṃ pāraṃ nāvam utsṛjya nirmamaḥ vyākhyātaṃ pūrvakalpena yathā rathipadātinau
english: Having crossed, free of the sense of mine, he abandons the boat and goes on to the farther shore. This has been explained by the earlier illustration, as of the chariot-rider and the man on foot.

sanskrit: snehāt saṃmoham āpanno nāvi dāśo yathā tathā mamatvenābhibhūtaḥ sa tatraiva parivartate
english: As the ferryman who out of attachment has fallen into delusion remains there upon his boat, so the man overcome by the sense of mine keeps turning about in that same place.

sanskrit: nāvaṃ na śakyam āruhya sthale viparivartitum tathaiva ratham āruhya nāpsu caryā vidhīyate
english: Having boarded a boat, one cannot move about upon dry land; even so, having mounted a chariot, no passage over the waters is ordained.

sanskrit: evaṃ karma kṛtaṃ citraṃ viṣayasthaṃ pṛthak pṛthak yathā karma kṛtaṃ loke tathā tad upapadyate
english: Thus the various deeds that are done, each set within its own sphere of objects, bear their fruit severally; as a deed is done in the world, so it comes to pass.

sanskrit: yan naiva gandhino rasyaṃ na rūpasparśaśabdavat manyante munayo buddhyā tat pradhānaṃ pracakṣate
english: That which has neither smell nor taste, neither form nor touch nor sound—this the sages perceive with their understanding and declare to be the Primordial Nature.

sanskrit: tatra pradhānam avyaktam avyaktasya guṇo mahān mahataḥ pradhānabhūtasya guṇo 'haṃkāra eva ca
english: Therein the Primordial Nature is the Unmanifest; the evolute of the Unmanifest is the Great Principle; and of the Great, become the foundation, the evolute is the I-sense itself.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārapradhānasya mahābhūtakṛto guṇaḥ pṛthaktvena hi bhūtānāṃ viṣayā vai guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: Of the I-sense, become the foundation, the evolute is what produces the great elements; for the sense-objects of the elements are severally held to be their qualities.

sanskrit: bījadharmaṃ yathāvyaktaṃ tathaiva prasavātmakam bījadharmā mahān ātmā prasavaś ceti naḥ śrutam
english: As the Unmanifest has the nature of a seed, so too it has the nature of bringing forth. We have heard that the Great Self has the nature of a seed and is also a bringer-forth.

sanskrit: bījadharmā tv ahaṃkāraḥ prasavaś ca punaḥ punaḥ bījaprasavadharmāṇi mahābhūtāni pañca vai
english: The I-sense too has the nature of a seed and brings forth again and again; and the five great elements have the nature both of seed and of bringing-forth.

sanskrit: bījadharmiṇa ity āhuḥ prasavaṃ ca na kurvate viśeṣāḥ pañcabhūtānāṃ teṣāṃ vittaṃ viśeṣaṇam
english: The particularized sense-objects of the five elements they call seed-natured, yet these do not bring forth further; know that they are but the distinguishing marks of those elements.

sanskrit: tatraikaguṇam ākāśaṃ dviguṇo vāyur ucyate triguṇaṃ jyotir ity āhur āpaś cāpi caturguṇāḥ
english: Therein ether has one quality, air is said to have two, fire they call possessed of three qualities, and water of four.

sanskrit: pṛthvī pañcaguṇā jñeyā trasasthāvarasaṃkulā sarvabhūtakarī devī śubhāśubhanidarśanā
english: Earth is to be known as having five qualities, teeming with things moving and unmoving, the goddess who fashions all beings, the revealer of the auspicious and the inauspicious.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśas tathā rūpaṃ raso gandhaś ca pañcamaḥ ete pañca guṇā bhūmer vijñeyā dvijasattamāḥ
english: Sound, touch, and form, taste, and smell as the fifth—these five are to be known as the qualities of earth, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: pārthivaś ca sadā gandho gandhaś ca bahudhā smṛtaḥ tasya gandhasya vakṣyāmi vistareṇa bahūn guṇān
english: Smell is ever earthly, and smell is held to be of many kinds; of that smell I shall declare in detail its many qualities.

sanskrit: iṣṭaś cāniṣṭagandhaś ca madhuro 'mlaḥ kaṭus tathā nirhārī saṃhataḥ snigdho rūkṣo viśada eva ca evaṃ daśavidho jñeyaḥ pārthivo gandha ity uta
english: Pleasant and unpleasant in smell, sweet, sour, and pungent, pervading, compact, oily, dry, and clear as well—thus earthly smell is to be known as of ten kinds.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśas tathā rūpaṃ rasaś cāpāṃ guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ rasajñānaṃ tu vakṣyāmi rasas tu bahudhā smṛtaḥ
english: Sound, touch, and form, and taste are held to be the qualities of water; but I shall declare the knowledge of taste, for taste is held to be of many kinds.

sanskrit: madhuro 'mlaḥ kaṭus tiktaḥ kaṣāyo lavaṇas tathā evaṃ ṣaḍvidhavistāro raso vārimayaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Sweet, sour, pungent, bitter, astringent, and salty—thus the taste born of water is held to be sixfold in its extent.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśas tathā rūpaṃ triguṇaṃ jyotir ucyate jyotiṣaś ca guṇo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ ca bahudhā smṛtam
english: Sound, touch, and form—fire is said to have three qualities; and the quality of fire is form, and form is held to be of many kinds.

sanskrit: śuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tathā raktaṃ nīlaṃ pītāruṇaṃ tathā hrasvaṃ dīrghaṃ tathā sthūlaṃ caturasrāṇu vṛttakam
english: White, black, and red, blue, yellow, and tawny; short, long, and thick, square, minute, and round—

sanskrit: evaṃ dvādaśavistāraṃ tejaso rūpam ucyate vijñeyaṃ brāhmaṇair nityaṃ dharmajñaiḥ satyavādibhiḥ
english: thus the form belonging to fire is said to be twelvefold in its extent, to be known ever by brāhmaṇas who know the law and speak the truth.

sanskrit: śabdasparśau ca vijñeyau dviguṇo vāyur ucyate vāyoś cāpi guṇaḥ sparśaḥ sparśaś ca bahudhā smṛtaḥ
english: Sound and touch are to be known as the two qualities by which air is said to be twofold; and the quality of air is touch, and touch is held to be of many kinds.

sanskrit: uṣṇaḥ śītaḥ sukho duḥkhaḥ snigdho viśada eva ca kaṭhinaś cikkaṇaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ picchilo dāruṇo mṛduḥ
english: Hot, cold, pleasant, painful, oily, and clear, hard, greasy, smooth, slimy, harsh, and soft—

sanskrit: evaṃ dvādaśavistāro vāyavyo guṇa ucyate vidhivad brahmaṇaiḥ siddhair dharmajñais tattvadarśibhiḥ
english: thus the quality belonging to air is said to be twelvefold in its extent, to be known duly by perfected brāhmaṇas who know the law and perceive the truth.

sanskrit: tatraikaguṇam ākāśaṃ śabda ity eva ca smṛtaḥ tasya śabdasya vakṣyāmi vistareṇa bahūn guṇān
english: Therein ether has one quality, and that is held to be sound; of that sound I shall declare in detail its many qualities.

sanskrit: ṣaḍjarṣabhau ca gāndhāro madhyamaḥ pañcamas tathā ataḥ paraṃ tu vijñeyo niṣādo dhaivatas tathā
english: Ṣaḍja and Ṛṣabha, Gāndhāra, Madhyama, and Pañcama, and beyond these are to be known Niṣāda and Dhaivata.

sanskrit: iṣṭo 'niṣṭaś ca śabdas tu saṃhataḥ pravibhāgavān evaṃ bahuvidho jñeyaḥ śabda ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ
english: Pleasant and unpleasant in tone, combined and divided—thus sound, which arises from ether, is to be known as of many kinds.

sanskrit: ākāśam uttamaṃ bhūtam ahaṃkāras tataḥ param ahaṃkārāt parā buddhir buddher ātmā tataḥ paraḥ
english: Ether is the highest of the elements; beyond it is the I-sense; higher than the I-sense is the intellect; and the Self is higher than the intellect.

sanskrit: tasmāt tu param avyaktam avyaktāt puruṣaḥ paraḥ parāvarajño bhūtānāṃ yaṃ prāpyānantyam aśnute
english: Higher than that is the Unmanifest, and higher than the Unmanifest is the Spirit, the knower of what is high and low among beings, on attaining whom one enjoys the Infinite.

sanskrit: brahmovāca bhūtānām atha pañcānāṃ yathaiṣām īśvaraṃ manaḥ niyame ca visarge ca bhūtātmā mana eva ca
english: Brahmā said: Now of these five elements the mind is the lord, both in restraint and in release; the mind is the very self of the elements.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhātā mano nityaṃ bhūtānāṃ mahatāṃ tathā buddhir aiśvaryam ācaṣṭe kṣetrajñaḥ sarva ucyate
english: The mind is ever the overseer of the great elements; the intellect proclaims their sovereignty; and the Knower of the Field is said to be the All.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi mano yuṅkte sadaśvān iva sārathiḥ indriyāṇi mano buddhiṃ kṣetrajño yuñjate sadā
english: The mind yokes the senses as a charioteer yokes good horses; and the Knower of the Field ever yokes the senses, the mind, and the intellect.

sanskrit: mahābhūtasamāyuktaṃ buddhisaṃyamanaṃ ratham tam āruhya sa bhūtātmā samantāt paridhāvati
english: The chariot is joined with the great elements and curbed by the intellect; having mounted it, the embodied self runs about on every side.

sanskrit: indriyagrāmasaṃyukto manaḥsārathir eva ca buddhisaṃyamano nityaṃ mahān brahmamayo rathaḥ
english: Joined with the host of the senses, having the mind for its charioteer and ever reined in by the intellect, the great chariot is made of Brahman.

sanskrit: evaṃ yo vetti vidvān vai sadā brahmamayaṃ ratham sa dhīraḥ sarvalokeṣu na moham adhigacchati
english: The wise man who thus ever knows this chariot made of Brahman—that steadfast one falls into no delusion in any of the worlds.

sanskrit: avyaktādi viśeṣāntaṃ trasasthāvarasaṃkulam candrasūryaprabhālokaṃ grahanakṣatramaṇḍitam
english: It begins with the Unmanifest and ends in the particulars; it teems with things moving and unmoving; it is a world lit by the radiance of moon and sun, adorned with planets and stars,

sanskrit: nadīparvatajālaiś ca sarvataḥ paribhūṣitam vividhābhis tathādbhiś ca satataṃ samalaṃkṛtam
english: everywhere graced with a network of rivers and mountains, and ever embellished with manifold waters,

sanskrit: ājīvaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ gatiḥ etad brahmavanaṃ nityaṃ yasmiṃś carati kṣetravit
english: the livelihood of all beings, the resort of all that bears the breath of life. This is the eternal forest of Brahman, in which the Knower of the Field roams.

sanskrit: loke 'smin yāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca tāny evāgre pralīyante paścād bhūtakṛtā guṇāḥ guṇebhyaḥ pañcabhūtāni eṣa bhūtasamucchrayaḥ
english: Whatever beings there are in this world, unmoving and moving, these dissolve first; afterward the qualities produced by the elements; from the qualities come the five elements—such is the upbuilding of beings.

sanskrit: devā manuṣyā gandharvāḥ piśācāsurarākṣasāḥ sarve svabhāvataḥ sṛṣṭā na kriyābhyo na kāraṇāt
english: Gods, men, and gandharvas, piśācas, asuras, and rākṣasas—all are created by their own inherent nature, not from rites and not from any other cause.

sanskrit: ete viśvakṛto viprā jāyante ha punaḥ punaḥ tebhyaḥ prasūtās teṣv eva mahābhūteṣu pañcasu pralīyante yathākālam ūrmayaḥ sāgare yathā
english: These makers of the universe, O brāhmaṇas, are born again and again; brought forth from them, they dissolve back into those very five great elements in due time, as waves dissolve into the sea.

sanskrit: viśvasṛgbhyas tu bhūtebhyo mahābhūtāni gacchati bhūtebhyaś cāpi pañcabhyo mukto gacchet prajāpatim
english: From the world-creating elements one passes to the great elements; and freed from the five elements, one may go on to Prajāpati.

sanskrit: prajāpatir idaṃ sarvaṃ tapasaivāsṛjat prabhuḥ tathaiva vedān ṛṣayas tapasā pratipedire
english: The Lord Prajāpati created this whole world by austerity alone; and even so the seers attained the Vedas through austerity.

sanskrit: tapasaś cānupūrvyeṇa phalamūlāśinas tathā trailokyaṃ tapasā siddhāḥ paśyantīha samāhitāḥ
english: And by the gradual practice of austerity, living on fruits and roots, the perfected ones, with concentrated minds, behold the triple world here through their austerity.

sanskrit: oṣadhāny agadādīnī nānāvidyāś ca sarvaśaḥ tapasaiva prasidhyanti tapomūlaṃ hi sādhanam
english: Herbs, antidotes, and the like, and the manifold sciences in every form, are perfected by austerity alone; for the means has austerity for its root.

sanskrit: yad durāpaṃ durāmnāyaṃ durādharṣaṃ duranvayam tat sarvaṃ tapasā sādhyaṃ tapo hi duratikramam
english: Whatever is hard to attain, hard to learn, hard to assail, hard to compass—all that may be accomplished by austerity; for austerity cannot be surpassed.

sanskrit: surāpo brahmahā steyī bhrūṇahā gurutalpagaḥ tapasaiva sutaptena mucyante kilbiṣāt tataḥ
english: The drinker of liquor, the slayer of a brāhmaṇa, the thief, the killer of an embryo, the violator of the teacher's bed—by austerity well practiced they are freed from their sin.

sanskrit: manuṣyāḥ pitaro devāḥ paśavo mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ yāni cānyāni bhūtāni trasāni sthāvarāṇi ca
english: Men, ancestors, and gods, cattle, beasts, and birds, and whatever other beings there are, moving and unmoving—

sanskrit: tapaḥparāyaṇā nityaṃ sidhyante tapasā sadā tathaiva tapasā devā mahābhāgā divaṃ gatāḥ
english: ever devoted to austerity, they attain perfection always through austerity; and even so the gods, those greatly fortunate ones, went to heaven by austerity.

sanskrit: āśīryuktāni karmāṇi kurvate ye tv atandritāḥ ahaṃkārasamāyuktās te sakāśe prajāpateḥ
english: But those who untiringly perform actions joined to desire for reward, bound up with the I-sense—they dwell in the presence of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: dhyānayogena śuddhena nirmamā nirahaṃkṛtāḥ prāpnuvanti mahātmāno mahāntaṃ lokam uttamam
english: By pure meditative yoga, free of the sense of mine and of the I-sense, the great-souled ones attain the great and supreme world.

sanskrit: dhyānayogād upāgamya prasannamatayaḥ sadā sukhopacayam avyaktaṃ praviśanty ātmavattayā
english: Coming through meditative yoga, ever serene in mind, they enter, by their command of self, into the Unmanifest, the storehouse of bliss.

sanskrit: dhyānayogād upāgamya nirmamā nirahaṃkṛtāḥ avyaktaṃ praviśantīha mahāntaṃ lokam uttamam
english: Coming through meditative yoga, free of the sense of mine and of the I-sense, they enter here into the Unmanifest, the great and supreme world.

sanskrit: avyaktād eva saṃbhūtaḥ samayajño gataḥ punaḥ tamorajobhyāṃ nirmuktaḥ sattvam āsthāya kevalam
english: Arisen from the Unmanifest itself, the knower of the right season returns again; released from darkness and passion, taking his stand on pure goodness alone,

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ sarvaṃ tyajati niṣkalaḥ kṣetrajña iti taṃ vidyād yas taṃ veda sa vedavit
english: freed from all sins, indivisible, he renounces all. One should know him as the Knower of the Field; and whoever knows him is a knower of the Veda.

sanskrit: cittaṃ cittād upāgamya munir āsīta saṃyataḥ yaccittas tanmanā bhūtvā guhyam etat sanātanam
english: Reaching pure thought from thought, let the sage sit restrained; becoming of one mind with that on which his thought is set—this is the eternal mystery.
